edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 in immediately available funds, without setoff, counterclaim, or deduction, in consideration for the Shares.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days after the date this Agreement is signed, or on such other date as the parties may agree in writing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement.
3. Representations. The Seller represents that, to the Seller’s knowledge, the financial statements delivered to the Buyer are accurate in all material respects as of their respective dates.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the existence and terms of this Agreement and any non-public information received from the other party in connection with the transaction, and shall not disclose such information except to its representatives who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations, as required by law, or with the other party’s prior written consent.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 43,000,000 in immediately available funds, without setoff, counterclaim, or deduction except as expressly provided in this Agreement. The purchase price and all other terms remain subject to the Buyer’s reasonable completion of due diligence and the parties’ agreement on definitive terms.

3. Representations and Warranties. The Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer, as of the date of this Agreement and as of Closing (except as expressly stated otherwise), that: (a) the Seller is duly organized and has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) this Agreement has been duly authorized and, when executed, will be binding on the Seller, subject to customary limitations under applicable insolvency laws and equitable principles; (c) the Seller owns the Shares, free and clear of liens created by the Seller, and has authority to transfer them; and (d) the financial statements delivered to the Buyer are accurate in all material respects as of their respective dates. The Seller’s representations and warranties shall be qualified by disclosures in the disclosure schedules to be agreed by the parties. The parties shall negotiate any additional customary representations and warranties, their scope and qualifications, and applicable survival periods in the definitive agreement.

Scope of any additional business, tax, compliance, employee, and other representations to be agreed following diligence, with customary disclosure schedules and appropriate materiality and knowledge qualifiers where applicable.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the existence and terms of this Agreement and any non-public information received from the other party in connection with the transaction, and shall not disclose such information except to its representatives who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations, as required by law, or with the other party’s prior written consent.

5. Indemnification and Remedies. The definitive agreement shall provide for customary indemnification by the Seller for losses arising from breaches of the Seller’s representations, warranties, and covenants, subject to negotiated notice and claims procedures, survival periods, a deductible or basket, a cap, and customary exclusions and limitations. The parties shall agree on the scope of recoverable losses and any exclusive-remedy provisions in the definitive agreement. No party may recover more than once for the same loss.

6. Conditions to Closing. Each party’s obligation to consummate the transaction shall be subject to customary conditions to be set forth in the definitive agreement, including the accuracy of the other party’s representations and warranties at the applicable time (subject to agreed materiality standards), performance in all material respects of its covenants, receipt of required governmental approvals, and absence of any order prohibiting Closing. The Buyer’s completion of due diligence shall be completed by a mutually agreed date and shall not constitute a discretionary condition to Closing except as expressly set forth in the definitive agreement.

7. Setoff. The Buyer may set off against amounts otherwise due to the Seller under this Agreement only amounts finally determined to be payable by the Seller to the Buyer pursuant to the definitive agreement or by a final, non-appealable judgment, in each case to the extent and subject to the procedures and limitations expressly negotiated in the definitive agreement.

partner.note_to_drafter: Remove the cover note before sending, or revise it to accurately describe the rendered draft. It refers to an indemnification framework that is not present. The draft does not disclose the confidential reservation price.

receiver.private_reasoning: The revised draft reduces the headline price by $2 million, but the Buyer should not accept $43 million as settled. The draft expressly leaves price and other terms subject to diligence and definitive agreement, so preserve that flexibility and seek a further reduction based on diligence. The expanded representations are a useful starting point, especially the unqualified material-accuracy statement about financial statements, but disclosures, additional reps, survival, and remedies remain unresolved. The setoff provision is highly restrictive and should be negotiated to allow good-faith claims and amounts due under agreed indemnity procedures, including escrow or deferred consideration if available. The document contains no comments, tracked changes, or hidden text. Its metadata appears routine and not revealing. No apparent inadvertent disclosure of confidential material is present.
receiver.observed_irregularities: No apparent improper or revealing material in the received document. No comments, tracked changes, or hidden text. Metadata identifies the drafting associate and contains ordinary document properties and timestamps; it does not appear to reveal confidential negotiation information.
receiver.requested_changes: Please confirm that the USD 43,000,000 figure is a proposal only and remains open pending diligence and definitive documentation. Given the remaining diligence and the unresolved allocation of risk, the Buyer cannot agree to that figure and proposes a lower purchase price, to be determined after review of the outstanding financial and operational materials. Preserve the unqualified financial-statement representation, and expand the Seller’s representations to cover, among other matters, capitalization and title to the Shares, authority, financial statements and liabilities, taxes, material contracts, compliance with law, litigation, employees, and absence of material adverse changes, with appropriately tailored qualifications and disclosure schedules. The definitive agreement should include meaningful survival periods and indemnification remedies, including recovery for breaches and a workable claims process. Revise Section 7 so setoff is not limited solely to amounts finally determined by non-appealable judgment or expressly negotiated final amounts; the Buyer should be able to set off amounts claimed in good faith under the definitive agreement, subject to agreed notice and dispute procedures, and against any deferred or contingent consideration. Include closing conditions satisfactory to the Buyer, including completion of diligence and absence of a material adverse change, and restore a mutual confidentiality provision with customary exceptions and permitted disclosures.
receiver.message_back: Thank you for the revised draft. We note the reduction to USD 43,000,000 and the addition of a broader framework. The Buyer is not in a position to accept that price or the proposed terms as final: diligence remains ongoing, and the draft itself contemplates further negotiation of definitive terms. Please treat the price as open; we will provide a specific counterproposal after reviewing the outstanding materials. The unqualified financial-statement representation is a constructive starting point. We would also like to discuss the additional representations, disclosure schedules, survival and indemnity framework, and Buyer-protective closing conditions. Section 7 should preserve a practical setoff right for good-faith claims under the definitive agreement, subject to agreed procedures, rather than making setoff available only after a final non-appealable judgment. Finally, please restore a mutual confidentiality provision. We look forward to continuing the discussion.
